## Introduction to backward kolmogorov equationss

The backwarda kolmogorov Equation deals with a terminal condition. The one dimensional backward
kolmogorov equation is going to deal with is of the form:

$$
\frac{\delta p}{\delta t} = -\mu(x) \frac{\delta p}{\delta x} + \frac{1}{2} \sigma^2(x) \frac{\delta^2 p}{\delta x^2},\enspace p(T, x) = \phi(x) \\
$$

$$
\forall t \in [0, T] \text{ and } x \in \mathbb{R}ᵈ
$$

In order to make the above equation in the form of Backward-Kolmogorov, we need to make a couple substitutions:
$$
\begin{aligned}
    & V(S, t) = e^r(t-T) p(S, t) \\
    & \text{thus we get} \\
    & e^r(t-T) \frac{\delta p}{\delta t} + r e^r(t-T) p(S, t) \\
    &= -\mu(x) \frac{\delta p}{\delta x} e^r(t-T) - \frac{1}{2} \sigma^2(x)\frac{\delta^2 p}{\delta x^2} e^r(t-T) + r e^r(t - T)p(S, t)
\end{aligned}
$$

```{julia}
# using Flux, NeuralPDE, Plots
using NeuralPDE, Plots
import Lux as Lx
import StochasticDiffEq as SDE

using Random, Statistics
using SciMLBase
using Optimization, OptimizationOptimisers
using Metal

# Metal.allowscaler(false)  # recommended to catch accidental CPU fallback

function maybe_gpu_metal(model, ps, st)
    if Metal.functional()    # :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index = 4}
        return Lx.fmap(Metal.mtl, model),
               Lx.fmap(Metal.mtl, ps),
               Lx.fmap(Metal.mtl, st),
               true
    end
        return model, ps, st, false
end

function maybe_cpu_metal(model, ps, st)
    # Metal.mtl oves CPU -> GPU; to come back, use Array conversion via fmap(Array, ...)
        return Lx.fmap(Array, model),
               Lx.fmap(Array, ps),
               Lx.fmap(Array, st)
end

#---------------#
# Compatibility
#---------------#
struct KolmogorovPDEProblem{F, G, PH}
        μ::F
        σ::G
        ϕ::PH
        xspan::Tuple{Float64, Float64}
        tspan::Tuple{Float64, Float64}
        d::Int
end

# MonteCarlo
function mc_target(prob::KolmogorovPDEProblem, x0::AbstractVector;
                   r::Float64,
                   sde_alg = SDE.EM(),
                   ensemble_alg = SDE.EnsembleThreads(),
                   dt::Float64 = 0.01,
                trajectories::Int = 100_000)
        sde_prob = SDE.SDEProblem(prob.μ, prob.σ, x0, prob.tspan)

        output_func(sol, i) = (sol[end], false)
        ens_prob = SDE.EnsembleProblem(sde_prob; output_func)

        sim = SDE.solve(ens_prob, sde_alg, ensemble_alg; dt=dt, trajectories
                = trajectories, adaptive = false)

        # sim.u is a vector of final states (each a Vector{Float64} of length d)
        S_T = reduce(hcat, sim.u)  # size: (d, trajectories)

        payoff_vals = vec(prob.ϕ(S_T))  # make sure its a vector!
        disc = exp(-r * (prob.tspan[2] - prob.tspan[1]))
        return disc * mean(payoff_vals)
end

# Batch generator for training
function make_training_data(prob::KolmogorovPDEProblem;
                            r::Float64,
                            ntrain::Int = 256,
                            dt::Float64 = 0.01,
                            trajectories::Int = 50_000,
                            rng::AbstractRNG = Random.default_rng())
    xs = rand(rng, ntrain) .* (prob.xspan[2] - prob.xspan[1]) .+ prob.xspan[1]
    X = reshape(xs, 1, :)  # (d=1, ntrain)

    y = Vector{Float64}(undef, ntrain)
    for (i, x) in enumerate(xs)
        y[i] = mc_target(prob, [x]; r=r, dt=dt, trajectories = trajectories)
    end
    Y = reshape(y, 1, :)  # (1, ntrain)
    return X, Y
end

# Train Lux model to fit MC targets
function train_nnk(prob::KolmogorovPDEProblem, model;
                   r::Float64,
                   ntrain::Int = 256,
                   dt::Float64 = 0.01,
                   trajectories::Int = 50_000,
                   lr::Float64 = 5e-4,
                   iters::Int = 2_000,
                   rng::AbstractRNG = Random.default_rng())

    X, Y = make_training_data(prob; r = r, ntrain = ntrain, dt=dt, trajectories
                              = trajectories, rng = rng)
    ps, st = Lx.setup(rng, model)
    model, ps, st, maybe_gpu_metal(model, ps, st)

    if use_gpu
        X = Metal.mtl(X)
        Y = Metal.mtl(Y)
    end

    function loss(pvec)
        yhat, _ = Lx.apply(model, Y, pvec, st)
        return mean((yhat .- Y).^2)
    end

    optf = OptimizationFunction((p, _) -> loss(p), Optimization.AutoZygote())
    optprob = OptimizationProblem(optf, ps)
    res = Optimization.solve(optprob, OptimizationOptimisers.Adam(lr); maxiters
                             = iters)

    ps_hat = res.u

    # bring back to cpu for plotting/downstream
    model, ps_hat, st = maybe_cpu_metal(model, ps_hat, st)
end
```

```{julia}
function phi(xi)
    y = Float64[]
    K = 100
    for x in eachcol(xi)
        val = max(K - maximum(x), 0.00)
        y = push!(y, val)
    end
    y = reshape(y, 1, size(y)[1])
    return y
end
```

To define the problem, we will need to define $\sigma$ and $\mu$ by comparing to the original equation. The xspan is the span of initial stock prices.

```{julia}
d     = 1
r     = 0.035
sigma = 0.2
xspan = (80.00, 115.00)
tspan = (0.0, 1.0)

σ(du, u, p, t) = (du .= sigma .* u)
μ(du, u, p, t) = (du .= r .* u)

prob = KolmogorovPDEProblem(μ, σ, phi, xspan, tspan, d)

sde_alg      = SDE.EM()
ensemble_alg = SDE.EnsembleThreads()
dt           = 0.01
trajectories = 100_000


# ---- Lux NN (flux-like architecture)
model = Lx.Chain(
    Lx.Dense(d, 64, Lx.elu),
    Lx.Dense(64, 128, Lx.elu),
    Lx.Dense(128, 16, Lx.elu),
    Lx.Dense(16, 1)
)

# ---- Train NN on MC targets sampled from xspan
model_tr, ps_tr, st_tr = train_nnk(prob, model; r = r, ntrain = 256, dt=dt,
                                   trajectories = 50_000, lr = 5e-4, iters
                                   = 2500)

# ---- MC curve on your x_out grid 
monte_carlo_sol = Float64[]
x_out = collect(85.0:2.0:110.0)

for x in x_out
    mean_phi = mc_target(prob, [x];
                         r=r,
                         sde_alg = sde_alg,
                         ensemble_alg = ensemble_alg,
                         dt = dt,
                         trajectories = trajectories)
    push!(monte_carlo_sol, mean_phi)
end

# ---- NN Curve
y_out = [predict(model_tr, ps_tr, st_tr, [x]) for x in x_out]

plot(x_out, y_out, lw=3, xaxis = "Initial Stock Price", yaxis = "Price", label = "NNKolmogorov
    (Lux)")
plot!(x_out, monte_carlo_sol, lw=3, label = "Monte Carlo Solutions")
```
